What: Building location and type (latitude, longitude, commercial / office / retail tag)
Where it comes from: OpenStreetMap, queried via the Overpass API. We pull buildings inside the bounding boxes of Miami-Dade, Broward, and Polk counties.
Why it matters: Real coordinates mean we are scoring real buildings in real neighborhoods, not points on an abstract grid.

What: Census tract assignment (the FIPS code that maps a coordinate to a neighborhood)
Where it comes from: FCC Area API. We give it a lat / lon, it returns the state, county, and tract code.
Why it matters: This is the bridge that lets us pull real neighborhood demographics for any random building we found on the map.

What: Median household income and minority percentage for the tract
Where it comes from: US Census Bureau, ACS 5-Year Estimates (2022). Specifically variables B19013_001E for income, and B02001_001E and B02001_002E for the racial composition.
Why it matters: These are the protected attributes the audit cares about. They are not used by the scoring AI directly, but they are what the fairness metric measures against.

What: FEMA flood zone (VE, AE, or X)
Where it comes from: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, queried via the ArcGIS REST API for the building's exact coordinates.
Why it matters: This is the strongest piece of physical risk data in the system. VE is the highest coastal hazard, AE is moderate, X is minimal.
